title: In-Memory Learning Automata Architecture using Y-Flash Cell
new_feature: Maps the full multi-state Tsetlin Automaton (not just its final action) onto the analog conductance of a single Y-Flash floating-gate memristor (180 nm CMOS), with 40 measured states (up to ~1000 with 10 us pulses), and uses an accumulating divergence counter (+-15 threshold) so the cell is only blind-written when accumulated TA state changes cross the threshold, enabling in-memory on-edge TM learning.

datasets.split_as_reported: training on 5000 data points; no test evaluation reported
datasets.notes: Used only to demonstrate mapping of TA state trajectories (8 TAs shown) onto Y-Flash writes; whether it is the noisy XOR variant is not stated. TA has 2N = 300 states, decision boundary at 150.

results.metric: write pulses to track TA trajectories
results.config: 8 TAs shown, 5000 training points, DC threshold +-15, pulse width 0.5 ms, 2N=300 TA states
results.notes: 4 of 8 TAs reached include; max included TA conductance 2.33 uS, min excluded 23.2 nS.

results.config: read at 2 V, 5 ns pulse, 40 states; average power 1.83 uW
program at 5 V, 200 us pulse, 40 states; average power 695 uW
erase at 8 V, 200 us pulse, 32 states; average power 8e-3 uW

extraction_notes: No classification accuracy, latency or throughput is reported; the paper is a device/mapping study. Device variability (C2C over 250 cycles: LCS 0.8-0.9 nS, HCS 1-1.08 uS; D2D over 100 devices: LCS mean 0.92 nS sd 0.047 nS, HCS mean 1.04 uS sd 0.027 uS; max program/erase time 8.6/11.2 ms) is summarised here rather than as results. Device-level energy results have dataset_id null. Table II confirmed from the PDF page render.
